caption:
You brace yourself every time someone corrects you. But what if the right rebuke is the very thing that saves you? (Galatians 2:11-14 devotional)

When Peter pulled back from the shared table, Paul opposed him to his face — not to wound him, but to keep the whole family from drifting into a quiet lie. A gospel rebuke isn't an attack; it's love refusing to let you go. Peter later called Paul "our beloved brother," proof that true correction ends in deeper family, not division.
